design:
Mock approved in look and structure by the operator (2026-11-10), built from real components fed fixtures: `cd hub/ui && npx vite --config vite.mock.config.ts`, then http://localhost:5199/mock.html#settings/general and #agent-settings/Builder/running. Screenshots: testbed/ui-judge/settings-style/ (dark and light, 1440 and 960). The components it renders are the deliverable; building is wiring them to the Hub's hooks.

Project settings, grouped in the side list:
- Project: Project (name, folder, delete), Collaboration, Permissions, Budgets (token limit, and the agent budget moved here)
- Agents: Instructions, Charters, Checkpoints, Manager
- Landing work: Checks (checks list, checks give way, generated files), Landing (main branch; pull requests and CI polling), Worktrees
- Specs and records: Spec steps, Traces, Diagnostics

Agent settings: Agent (identity + charter), Running (model + waits), Permissions (default permissions, granted reach, access grants), Checkpoints, Workspace. App settings unchanged.

Save rule (operator, 2026-11-10: "leave the button behaviour only where it's needed"): a setting applies on change; long text applies when its field is left. Instructions keeps its Save, because saving commits AGENTS.md and emptying it asks to confirm.

Model choice: the menu value is provider plus model, as agent creation already accepts (AgentCreate's provider+model form). The Hub binds the agent to a runner of that provider and model, reusing one if it exists. Runners stay the Hub's: checkpoint and manager menus still list them.

Components already written for the mock (hub/ui/src/components/settings/: GeneralSettings.tsx section exports, SpecStepsSettings.tsx, TracesSettings.tsx, CommittedTextarea in CommittedInput.tsx, SettingsNavLayout groups; hub/ui/src/components/agents/settings/: AgentSettingsPages.tsx, AgentPermissionGroup and AgentAccessGroups in AgentSettingsSections.tsx). They type-check and lint clean, and the existing settings and agent tests pass (639) with them in place.

Hazard: the UI bundle is committed and reaches the operator's :8000 on reload once master is merged; each task rebuilds it, so the tasks are chained rather than parallel.

problem:
Code as of master 35c13ea (2026-11-10), after slice 1 shipped:

- Project settings → General (ProjectSettingsScreen.tsx: GeneralSection, then SpecStepsSection, then TracesSection) renders seven groups on one page about 5,700px tall: Collaboration (jobs allowed, hop budget, deliveries per turn, agent budget, token limit), Reach (default permissions, granted reach), Integration (main branch, checks, checks give way, generated files, PR landing, one commit per build, PR CI is the full check, CI check names, CI polling interval and cutoff), Checkpointing (six rows), Project (name, folder, delete). Spec steps and Traces then follow the danger zone.
- Quality (QualityHealthPanel) shows only a pointer to agentweave.yml, a file the product no longer uses.
- Runners (RunnersSection, RunnerForm) is the only place a runner is created, edited (CLI, model, flags) or deleted. The operator has never used it (2026-11-10). On their own Hub every runner is either one of the three seeded defaults (db/engine.py `_seed_default_runners`) or one created by choosing a provider and model when an agent was created (AgentCreate's provider+model form). None has flags (read-only query of ~/.agentweave/hub/data/agentweave.db, 13 runners in 3 projects). An agent's Execution → Runner menu lists only runners that already exist.
- There are three save models. Most rows save on change. Generated files and trace retention each have their own Save. Spec steps has "Save steps". Traces has "Save export settings". Instructions has one Save for its text body.
- Two row systems are still in use. Agent settings (AgentSettingsPage, AgentSettingsControls), Spec steps, Traces and the Quality panel use the older `settings-row` from environment/SettingsSection.tsx. Everything else uses `SettingsRow` (components/ui/settings.tsx).
- Some controls are native rather than the app's primitives: checkboxes in Spec steps (step sizes), Traces ("Send to a collector") and agent settings; date inputs in Traces' export range; <select>s in Spec steps ("Add after") and agent Context (checkpoint mode, unit). Built-in spec steps are titled by their raw slug ("requirements-and-acceptance").
- Agent settings has seven sections (Identity, Execution, Charter, Interaction, Context, Access, Workspace) holding about fifteen rows; Charter is one row, Interaction two, and an agent's default permissions sit under Execution while what it may read and decide sits under Access.
- App settings has three sections (Sound and notifications, Appearance, Hub connection) that read clearly; they stay as they are.

requirements.rationale: The operator approved this list and grouping in the mock (2026-11-10). General held seven groups on one ~5,700px page, so nothing on it was where its name said.
requirements.statement: Project settings lists exactly these sections, under these group headings, in this order: Project — Project, Collaboration, Permissions, Budgets; Agents — Instructions, Charters, Checkpoints, Manager; Landing work — Checks, Landing, Worktrees; Specs and records — Spec steps, Traces, Diagnostics. No section named General, Quality or Runners is listed.

requirements.rationale: A reorganisation that drops a setting is a regression nobody sees until they need it.
requirements.statement: Every setting the General page held appears on exactly one project settings section: name, folder and delete on Project; jobs allowed, hop budget and deliveries per turn on Collaboration; default permissions and granted reach on Permissions; agent budget and token limit on Budgets; the six checkpoint settings on Checkpoints; checks, checks give way and generated files on Checks; main branch, pull-request landing, one commit per build, PR CI as the full check, CI check names, CI interval and CI cutoff on Landing.

requirements.rationale: Links to settings exist in toasts, notices and other screens (General's token limit, a runner error); a removed id must not open a blank page.
requirements.statement: A link or saved location naming a section that no longer exists opens its successor: General, Quality and Runners open Project; an agent's Identity or Charter opens Agent, Execution or Interaction opens Running, Access opens Permissions, Context opens Checkpoints.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-10: a Save stays only where it is needed. Saving Instructions writes and commits AGENTS.md and emptying it asks to confirm, so it is an act rather than a stored value. Confirm buttons inside dialogs (add a check, replace headers, clear traces) are actions, not saves.
requirements.statement: Every setting on project and agent settings applies when it is changed — a text or number field when it is left or Enter is pressed, a long text when it is left — and no section shows a Save button for a setting, except Instructions, which keeps its one Save.
No project or agent settings section renders a native checkbox, a native <select> or a native date input; each such choice uses the app's own switch, toggle, menu or segmented control.

Spec steps shows the steps in order, each built-in step under a title in words (Intake, Requirements, Requirements and acceptance, Acceptance criteria, Approach, Tasks, Build) and marked built in; adding a step, moving or removing one of the operator's steps, changing its sizes, or changing any step's added instruction or a custom step's instructions applies at once, and a change the Hub refuses shows the Hub's reason and leaves the list as the Hub last stored it.

Traces applies the retention, the collector switch and the endpoint on change; replaces the collector headers only through a dialog, never displaying a stored value; and downloads or clears the traces of the last 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days or all of them, as chosen, with clearing confirmed first.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-10. Permissions and Checkpoints share their names with the project sections they override, which slice 3's inheritance display builds on.
requirements.statement: An agent's settings list exactly five sections — Agent (name, description, last active, charter, archive), Running (model, permission-decision wait, question wait, and Copilot's extras for a Copilot agent), Permissions (default permissions, own granted reach, reading other agents' checkpoints, recall, deciding evidence, keeping the specs true), Checkpoints (checkpoint mode, its own checkpoint point, its checkpoints taken) and Workspace (working directory, its own checkout, provider sessions).

requirements.rationale: With no Runners screen, a menu of existing runners could never reach a model nobody had used yet. Reusing runners keeps the checkpoint and manager menus, which still list runners, from filling with duplicates.
requirements.statement: An agent's Running → Model lists every model of every provider whose coding agent is installed, plus each provider's own default, and choosing one makes the agent's next turn run on that provider and model without a runner having been created first; the Hub reuses an existing runner of the same provider and model rather than adding a second one.
Where an agent has no value of its own for a checkpoint setting or a permission, its section says what the project's value is, and a reset returns it to following the project.
The long-values check from `settings-rows-that-hold-any-value` passes on every new project and agent section at 960 and 1440px, dark and light.
The built screens match the mock the operator approved on 2026-11-10 (hub/ui/mock, routes settings/* and agent-settings/*), and the operator signs them off against the rest of the app.

summary: Reorganise project and agent settings so a setting sits where its name says, matching the mock the operator approved on 2026-11-10. In project settings, General is split into named sections, Spec steps and Traces get their own, and Quality and Runners are removed. Agent settings go from seven sections to five, and an agent picks its model directly. Every setting saves on change except Instructions. Every control is one of the app's own.
